tools.name: search_businesses
tools.description: Searches businesses that have chosen to be discoverable on Are We Working, by name or handle. Returns each match's handle, city and state (to tell apart businesses with the same name), and current status. Businesses that are not listed will not appear here, but can still be looked up with get_busine

tools.name: get_status_history
tools.description: Returns the most recent status changes for a business, newest first, each with the status, note, and time. Useful for 'when did it close?' or 'how often does this change?'.

tools.name: get_alert_signup_link
tools.description: Returns the business's status page link, where the person can tap 'Get alerts' to sign up themselves. Use this for TEXT alerts: text opt-in must be completed by the person on the web form, not by an agent. Text alerts may not be enabled yet.

tools.name: request_email_alerts
tools.description: Signs a person up to receive an email whenever a business's status changes. findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "get_business_status" stacks urgency/override words (immediately, warning). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: request_email_alerts · Public sink: request_email_alerts.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: request_email_alerts · Public sink: request_email_alerts

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
